name: Alaska

agency.name: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

overview: ADF&G awards drawing permits by a random computer lottery with no preference or bonus points, from one application period each year (November 1 - December 15, 2026 for 2027 hunts; results on the third Friday of February). Applicants may submit up to six applications per species at $5 each ($10 for bison and muskox), and most drawing hunts are open to residents and nonresidents, although many are limited to one residency and nonresidents hunting Dall sheep, mountain goat or brown/grizzly bear need an Alaska-licensed guide or a resident relative within the second degree of kindred. Much Alaska big game hunting needs no drawing: general seasons use free harvest tickets, registration permits are issued over the counter, and residents can apply for Tier I/II subsistence permits, which are scored rather than drawn at random. Caribou, bison, muskox, wolf and brown/grizzly bear are hunted in Alaska but are not covered here.

species.drawSystemSummary: ADF&G awards drawing permits by a computer lottery: each valid application gets a random draw number for each hunt and permits go to the lowest numbers; there are no preference or bonus points. An applicant may submit up to six applications per species ($5 each), may apply for the same hunt more than once, may apply alone or as a two-person party, and may not be awarded the same drawing hunt two years in a row. Moose are also hunted on general-season harvest tickets, registration permits and, for residents, scored Tier I/II subsistence permits.
species.residentNote: Residents need a hunting license but no moose locking-tag. Tier II moose permits (for example TM059, TM565) are for Alaska residents only and are awarded by application score, not by lottery; only one Tier II moose permit per household.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents must buy a moose locking-tag ($800; $1,000 for nonresident aliens, who must hunt with an Alaska-licensed guide). Many drawing hunts are limited to residents or to nonresidents, and some to guided or nonguided nonresidents.
species.otcSummary: General-season moose hunts need only a free harvest ticket, and many registration permits are issued without a drawing; nonresidents buy the moose locking-tag over the counter.

species.drawSystemSummary: Sitka black-tailed deer (Odocoileus hemionus sitkensis) are hunted in general seasons on free harvest tickets; the 2022-2023 through 2027-2028 drawing supplements list no deer drawing hunts.
species.residentNote: Residents need a hunting license and free deer harvest tickets, used in sequential order.
species.nonresidentNote: Nonresidents need a deer locking-tag ($300; $400 nonresident alien) and harvest tickets.
species.otcSummary: Deer harvest tickets are free from license vendors, ADF&G offices and online; nonresident deer locking-tags are sold over the counter.

coverage.notes: Counts are ADF&G's per-hunt drawing results: Apps Received (applications, not unique applicants: one hunter may apply for the same hunt more than once and a party application covers two hunters) as total.applicants, Permits Available as total.quota, and % Drawn as published (whole percent; '<1' stored as null with a row note). No resident/nonresident split and no point data are published. Drawing year Y = applications Nov-Dec of Y-1, results in February of Y, hunts in the Y-(Y+1) regulatory year; counts from the back page of the (Y+1)-(Y+2) supplement, hunt details from the Y-(Y+1) supplement. Tier I/II subsistence, registration and general-season (harvest ticket) hunts are not drawings and are not in these rows. Caribou (DC/YC), bison (DI), muskox (DX) and emperor goose (DO) drawing hunts, brown/grizzly bear (DB) and wolf are not covered (no HuntScout species key). Includes youth drawing hunts (YM). Hunts DM802-DM811 (Unit 21B Nowitna River, 2023-2026) and DM766 (Unit 20A Wood River CUA East, 2022-2025) are printed in tables whose cells could not be separated, so those rows carry only the GMU/area label and the counts. Season dates are omitted for 49 moose rows and the legal animal for 61 where the supplement cell could not be read unambiguously (mostly 2022 Unit 14A and the hunts above); JBER (14C) weapon certifications are printed in rotated text and are not captured.
